title: Jollof Dry Spice Mix
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: Thirty grams each of ground ginger and dried thyme lead a mix that also carries cinnamon, nutmeg and cubeb tail pepper.
longDesc: The dry mix that the jollof sauce and the one-pot rice are both seasoned with, and it is unusual in reaching for cinnamon, nutmeg and coriander alongside the ginger and thyme. Thirty grams of ground ginger, sixteen of garlic powder, ten of ground onion, five of smoked paprika, twenty of dried chilli flakes, thirty of dried thyme, and twelve and a half grams each of cinnamon, nutmeg and coriander, with sea salt, cubeb tail pepper and optional dried prawn powder. Blend it all in a spice grinder or pestle, store airtight in a cool dark place, and use within a few months.
ingredients: 1 tsp freshly ground cubeb tail pepper
Scant 1 tsp dried ground prawn, shrimp or crayfish powder (optional)
equipment: Spice grinder or pestle and mortar
steps: Blend them together in a spice grinder or pestle.
Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place.
chefTips: Cubeb tail pepper is the unusual one — Piper cubeba, a tailed peppercorn with a resinous, allspice-like note. Nothing substitutes precisely; black pepper is the nearest.
Thirty grams each of ginger and thyme makes those two the backbone. Everything else sits under them.
Use within a few months, by her own instruction. Ground spices at this scale lose their edge.
The optional prawn powder makes the mix non-vegetarian, so leave it out if that matters and the mix still works.
Be aware there are two published printings and they differ substantially — this one has onion, paprika and cubeb, the other has none of those and adds black pepper instead.
The second printing's weights also sum to a hundred and sixty grams against a printed yield of about a hundred and ninety, which does not add up. Treat yields in this family loosely.
Make it before you make either the jollof sauce or the one-pot rice, since both call for it by the tablespoon.
commonMistakes: Substituting black pepper for cubeb without noticing the difference.
Keeping it more than a few months.
Mixing the two printings' proportions together.
Storing it somewhere warm or light.
Including the prawn powder in a vegetarian dish.
sources: TWO PRINTINGS EXIST AND THEY DISAGREE. The version published above is printing (a).

(a) stylist.co.uk, 5 February 2021. BYLINE FLAG: one fetch printed 'By Stylist Team' and another 'Author: Zoe Adjonyoh'; the intro says 'chef Zoe Adjonyoh shares three of her favourite recipes', so the byline is treated as Stylist Team with the recipe credited to Adjonyoh. The spice mix is attributed on the page to 'Zoe says'. Quantities TWO-PASS. Ingredients exactly as printed: 30g ground ginger; 16g garlic powder; 10g ground onion; 5g smoked paprika; 20g dried chilli flakes; 30g dried thyme; 12.5g ground cinnamon; 12.5g ground nutmeg; 12.5g ground coriander; 1 tsp sea salt; 1 tsp freshly ground cubeb tail pepper; scant 1 tsp dried ground prawn/shrimp or crayfish powder (optional). METHOD, verbatim: 'Blend all the ingredients together in a spice grinder or pestle. Store in an airtight container in a cool, dark place and use within a few months.'

(b) dailymaverick.co.za, 31 March 2021. BYLINE FLAG: one fetch printed 'By The Reading List' and another 'By Zoe Adjonyoh'; the verbatim reading is 'By The Reading List', so that is recorded as the page byline with the recipe credited 'from Zoe's Ghana Kitchen (Octopus, R515)'. Quantities TWO-PASS. 'Makes about 190g': 25g ground ginger; 25g garlic powder; 20g dried chilli flakes; 35g dried thyme; 25g ground cinnamon; 15g ground nutmeg; 15g ground coriander; ¼ teaspoon cooking salt; ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper; scant 1 teaspoon dried ground prawn/shrimp or crayfish powder (optional).
AN ARITHMETIC PROBLEM IN PRINTING (b), flagged and NOT corrected: its listed weights sum to about 160 g against a printed yield of 'about 190g'. The thirty grams unaccounted for are not explained.

THE DISAGREEMENT, unreconciled: printing (a) contains GROUND ONION, SMOKED PAPRIKA and CUBEB TAIL PEPPER, which (b) lacks entirely; (b) adds BLACK PEPPER, which (a) lacks. Their shared spices also differ in weight — ginger 30 g against 25 g, garlic 16 g against 25 g, thyme 30 g against 35 g, cinnamon 12.5 g against 25 g, nutmeg and coriander 12.5 g against 15 g. Salt goes from a full teaspoon to a quarter. These are materially different blends and neither is corrected toward the other.

ON CUBEB TAIL PEPPER: Piper cubeba, a tailed peppercorn from Java with a resinous, allspice-and-pepper character, historically traded through West Africa. Its presence in printing (a) and absence in (b) is the single biggest flavour difference between the two.

WHY THIS ENTRY MATTERS BEYOND ITSELF: both the jollof sauce (GHA100) and the jollof one-pot rice (GHA099) call for this mix by the tablespoon, and the jollof fried chicken (GHA102) takes two tablespoons of it. Which printing you make therefore changes three other dishes.
NO SERVING SIZE is printed. The twenty servings above is an editorial division of roughly 190 g at a heaped tablespoon per use.
storage: A few months in an airtight container in a cool dark place, per the author.
healthBenefits: Ginger, cinnamon and thyme all carry documented anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial compounds.
Vegan without the optional prawn powder.
Replaces salt-heavy bouillon in several dishes.
culturalNote: Cinnamon, nutmeg and cubeb in a jollof seasoning look surprising until you remember that West Africa was a spice-trading coast long before it was a colony — grains of paradise went north across the Sahara and cubeb came the other way. A diaspora cook formalising all of it into a weighed blend is how that history gets kept usable.
